column5: regmove will not tie an AND to a parameter copy unless the next insn sets it again: mask and shift the parameter in place (flags &= m; flags >>= 12), then a separate priority = flags - 1.
A chain of early returns (if (!p) return 0; ...) with one object = input copy read only by the last test keeps both pointer registers; nested ifs and && chains let cse merge them.
The graphic index is narrowed in the call: (u16)(entry->graphic + 0x121); the truncation that combine later proves redundant keeps the constant load and copy apart from the byte.

A plain for loop that indexes a parts base pointer declared in the body (parts[i]) plus an inline SetAction(state, 1, 5) helper gives the hoisted constants and giv order; the hand-rotated pointer walk needed the pin.

Same indexed for loop; the queue-part step is an inline helper whose body is the shared ARMOR_QUEUE_PART_ACTION statement macro, which doubles the count pointer refs (the r3/r4 order) and leaves the dead zero pseudo that owns r8.

cse (fold_rtx) always moves a register with a known constant second, so the ROM order base+offset needs the base set outside the add's cse block (cse stops at a NOTE_INSN_LOOP_END, i.e. a statement macro around the base setup); no shared macro is evident for it.
A two-case switch written case 23 then case 10 gives the ROM's layout, and a second manager view pointer read only in the case 10 arm (reached through a label) keeps the early r1-to-r3 copy.
Two plain for loops over one index; the byte is updated in place with two compound assignments (buffer[i] ^= word; buffer[i] &= mask), which loop.c turns into the pointer walk and countdown itself.
Plain field code: p->flags88 |= 2; p->flags88 &= ~1; as two statements (README fact 103) gives the or-with-zero, and the literal 1 is shared by cse; no named constants needed.
Field code with no locals: if (++particle->frame > 15), offsetY += velocityY, and the phase test read from particle->frame again; cse supplies the registers the pins forced.

ROM keeps p in r4 for the inlined hit test and a top-of-function copy in r5 for the tail; cse makes the copy the class head and deletes p in every ordinary form tried (copy, inline, early returns, goto).
One slot variable carries the next window, then its previous-link address, then the window's own previous slot after the join; with separate variables the allocator puts next in r1.

Without the r0 pin the sample and the coordinate swap r0/r2: local-alloc ranks the coordinate quantity (12 refs) above the sample (8 refs) in every ordinary form tried (types, operand order, shared or per-block variables).

Plain for loop over slots[i] with the first slot's flags test kept as written and an inline helper for the delay and flag stores; the pins were holding three hand-made pointers that loop creates by itself.

Plain loop is right except loop hoists the activeCount address on its second pass (15*life 3 >= 39 insns); the ROM recomputes it each iteration, so its loop body had more RTL insns or a shorter-lived address than any ordinary form tried (bitfield flag, inline forms, continue).

One function-scope id variable shared by all three cases (the index in case 0, the category*6+index result in cases 1 and 2) with block-local category and index; the shared pseudo is what blocks r1/r2 and pushes menu and pending to r3/r4.

All but one insn fall out of plain code (pressed = MASK; pressed &= keys); the first test needs RTL (and one keys) with the 1 not known constant to cse, which swaps it in every ordinary form (shared variable, types, loop wrappers).

Plain early returns, a for loop and bitfield stores match once the slot is read from the trigger again after the inline status test and before the branch (comma expression); the pin and barriers were forcing those two copies.

An inline SetFlags(actor, mask) gives the mask-first OR, leaving only the second pointer register: cse carries actor==p around the skipped if-blocks to the last call and merges them; the ROM path was cut at the first if (a join label with two uses does it, e.g. changed && x, but no form without an extra test was found). Same cause as WoodenCrate_ReactToHit.

Plain do-while with five mask locals before the loop and nested tests gets the shape, but four allocation details stay off (flags copy to r4 before the first branch, state address kept in r1, 120 not hoisted, zero in r1); each needs its own lever and no ordinary form covered all.

Plain if/else with inline helpers; the status helper returns u8 through two returns, whose zero-extension keeps jump from threading the status==0 path (what the barrier forced), and show/hide written in each branch cross-jump on their own.

Plain field code with volatile frame/interval fields and a u16 frame local gets every instruction; five pool-constant offset loads take other registers (r3/r1 where the draft has r0/r1/r2), a reload spill-rotation difference that one rotation shift does not explain.
The loop reads the saved id from the game state twice (test, then argument) with no local; the pins were holding a hand-built row pointer and id register.

Literal `& 31` masks (HImode for the shifted components) let loop hoist both masks and give the ROM registers with no pin, but the red AND then ties to the color instead of a copy of the mask (4 insns); the mask-first order needs a mask cse cannot see as constant.

The dead abs code is four identical-call arms (`if (ax > az) { if (x > 0) F; else F; } else if (z > 0) F; else F;`) merged by jump2 after flow, which gives the ROM registers with no barrier; three arms merge but the last arm call falls into the join label, gets flow (use 0) nop and stays apart (12 extra insns).

An inline that reads actor->direction and writes variant/mirror through pointers, plus a u8 local for mirror | entry->flags (its extra zero-extend flips combine's operand swap back and keeps the two byte loads as QI pseudos), replaces both pins.

The sibling inline form does not carry over: the ROM copies the mirror pointer to a second register after the quadrant is computed and reloads the variant address from sp, which the natural inline (or a nested one) does not reproduce; the DEBUG_NOP between the two entry loads is still needed.
The dead movs r7,#0 is a zero flag operand ORed into child->flags inside the loop: set before the loop, it survives flow and combine folds its use afterwards (scope fact 94), so no r7 pin is needed.
Same child-callback loop as Actor_UpdateBlinkBurstDisappearance: a zero flag operand in the loop replaces the r7 pin.

Reload's spill rotation was one step off: the first random draw indexes the table at its literal address (RANDOM_TABLE_ADDR), so reload loads that constant and the later ldrsh index lands in r2 with no r1 pin.

local-alloc: without the pin the callback address takes r0 (free after the 0xFFFF store) where the ROM has r1; not a reload choice (spill finds no shift), and no ordering of the two stores or helper form moved it.

global-alloc liveness: 0x2f0 (the action offset, reused by cse as the case 2 collision mask) must be live through case 1 so the shared 0x3FF mask takes ip instead of sl; the barrier at the end supplies that use and no natural later use of the value was found.

local-alloc's three-quantity sort compares by index and misorders the block; a block-local display pointer in the else branch makes a fourth quantity, qsort then orders by priority and the plain flags |= 1 gets the ROM registers with no pin (the capture macro goes too).

cse copy propagation: the ROM keeps a second register copy of name (r6) for two of the tag compares and goes back to r4 after; a plain local copy is folded into name by cse (name is the older equivalent with the later last use), so only the pin keeps it.

cse equivalence: agbcc expands each struct byte store as (old & 0) | value, and the ROM's early movs r1,#0 is the first store's mask zero that cse keeps for the later zero stores while target->pendingFlag gets its own; every plain form shares the zeros differently (best: 1 insn, a zero local set before the clamp). Same cause as QueueIncomingItem, QueueLocalItem and UpdateIncomingItem in this unit.

cse equivalence (same as UpdateItemMerge): the zero loaded before each count store is the byte store's mask zero; a plain rewrite with field code gets the shape but not which stores share it, and the argument copies to high registers also move.
